sections.title: リーディング・ライティング

items.q: Please be careful. The floor is still wet, so it's very (　).
items.ex: slippery で「すべりやすい」。床がぬれているので注意をうながしています。

items.q: The concert was (　) because of the heavy snow. All tickets will be refunded.
items.ex: チケットが払い戻される=コンサートが「中止された」canceled。

items.q: Kana has a strong (　) to become a doctor, so she studies science every night.
items.ex: desire で「強い願い、望み」。a desire to ～ で「～したいという願い」。

items.q: The teacher asked us to (　) the main points of the story in three sentences.
items.ex: summarize で「要約する」。3文でまとめるので summarize。

items.q: This old castle is one of the most famous (　) in the area. Many tourists visit it every year.
items.ex: sights で「名所、観光地」。

items.q:
A: How was your job interview?
B: I was so nervous that I could (　) speak at first.
items.ex: hardly で「ほとんど～ない」。緊張して最初はほとんど話せなかった、です。

items.q: The price of vegetables has (　) a lot because of the bad weather this summer.
items.ex: 「(値段が)上がる」は rise(自動詞)。現在完了なので has risen。raise は「～を上げる」(他動詞)です。

items.q: Lisa (　) the train by one minute, so she had to wait thirty minutes for the next one.
items.ex: miss the train で「電車に乗りおくれる」。

items.q: The doctor told my father to (　) smoking for his health.
items.ex: give up ～ing で「～するのをやめる」。

items.q: We need to (　) a decision by tomorrow, so let's talk about it now.
items.ex: make a decision で「決定する」。

items.q: Thanks to the new highway, it now takes (　) time to get to the airport than before.
items.ex: time は数えられない名詞で、than があるので比較級 less。fewer は数えられる名詞に使います。

items.q: The museum guide spoke so fast that I couldn't keep (　) with her explanation.
items.ex: keep up with ～ で「～についていく」。

items.q: If it (　) tomorrow, the soccer game will be canceled.
items.ex: 条件を表す if の文では、未来のことでも現在形を使います。

items.q: Neither my father (　) my mother can drive a car.
items.ex: neither A nor B で「AもBも～ない」。

items.q: The movie was (　) boring that I fell asleep in the middle.
items.ex: so ～ that … で「とても～なので…」。such のあとには名詞が必要です。

items.q: I'm looking forward to (　) you at the party next week.
items.ex: look forward to ～ing で「～するのを楽しみにする」。to のあとは動名詞。

items.q: Ms. Green made her students (　) the classroom after the event.
items.ex: make + 人 + 動詞の原形 で「人に～させる」。

blocks.label: [A]
blocks.title: A Library of Things
blocks.body:
Many people own tools and machines that they rarely use. For example, an electric drill is used for only a very short time during its whole life. To solve this problem, some cities have opened a "library of things." Instead of books, these libraries lend out items such as tools, tents, and sewing machines. Members ( 18 ) for a few days and then return them.
These libraries have several benefits. Members can save money because they do not have to buy expensive items. They can also ( 19 ), because their homes will not be filled with things they hardly use. In addition, fewer products need to be made, which is better for the environment.
Some people, however, worry that borrowed items might be broken or dirty. ( 20 ), the libraries check every item when it is returned and clean it before lending it out again.

qs.ex: 図書館なので、会員は数日間「物を借りて」返します。
「家があまり使わない物でいっぱいにならない」ので、「スペースを節約できる」。
「こわれている・汚れているかも」という心配に対して、点検・掃除をしている=「この心配に対応するため」。

blocks.label: [B]
blocks.title: Why Teenagers Stay Up Late
blocks.body:
Many teenagers find it difficult to get up early in the morning. Parents often think that their children are just lazy. However, scientists say that ( 21 ). During the teenage years, the body starts to produce a sleep hormone later at night than it does in children and adults. As a result, many teenagers do not feel sleepy until around 11 p.m.
Because most schools start early, many teenagers do not get enough sleep. This can make it hard for them to ( 22 ) during class. Some studies have also found that students who sleep too little are more likely to feel stressed.
For this reason, some schools in the United States have changed their start time from around 7:30 a.m. to 8:30 a.m. ( 23 ), students at these schools slept longer, and their attendance and grades improved.

o: teenagers need less sleep than adults
there is a natural reason for this
getting up early is good for health
parents should wake their children earlier
qs.ex: However(しかし)のあと、睡眠ホルモンが夜おそく出るという「体の自然な理由」を説明しています。
睡眠不足で授業中に「集中する」のがむずかしくなる。
始業時刻を変えた「あとで」、睡眠時間が増え、出席や成績が良くなりました。

blocks.label: [A]
blocks.body:
From: Laura Bennett
To: Aoi Tanaka
Date: March 8
Subject: Your homestay in Vancouver

Dear Aoi,
We are so excited that you will be staying with us this summer! My husband, Mark, and I have two children: Ethan, who is 12, and Chloe, who is 9. We also have a dog named Max. You said in your letter that you are a little afraid of big dogs. Don't worry. Max is small and very gentle, and he usually sleeps all day.
Your room is on the second floor, and it has a desk where you can study. Your school is about 30 minutes away by bus. On your first day, Mark will drive you there so that you can learn the way. After that, you can take the bus by yourself.
We are planning a camping trip to a lake on your second weekend. Do you have a sleeping bag? If not, we can lend you one. Also, please let me know if there is any food you cannot eat.
See you soon!
Laura

o: He needs someone to walk him every day.
Aoi said she is a little afraid of big dogs.
Ethan wants Aoi to play with him.
Max will go camping with them.
qs.ex: You said in your letter that you are a little afraid of big dogs. Don't worry. とあります。

qs.q: How will Aoi get to school on her first day?
qs.ex: On your first day, Mark will drive you there とあります。バスは2日目からです。

qs.q: What does Laura ask Aoi to tell her?
o: If there is any food she cannot eat.
When she will arrive in Vancouver.
If she can bring a tent.
Which school she wants to go to.
qs.ex: please let me know if there is any food you cannot eat とあります。

blocks.label: [B]
blocks.title: Reading with Fingers
blocks.body:
Braille is a system of raised dots that allows people who cannot see to read with their fingers. Each letter is made of up to six dots arranged in two lines of three. By feeling which dots are raised, readers can recognize letters, numbers, and even musical notes.
The system was invented by Louis Braille, a French boy who lost his sight after an accident when he was a small child. At his school for blind children in Paris, books were printed with large raised letters, which were heavy and very slow to read. When Louis was 12, he learned about a system of dots that soldiers had used to read messages at night without light. He thought the idea was useful but too complicated, so he spent the next few years making it simpler. By the age of 15, he had created the basic system that is still used today.
At first, many teachers did not accept Louis's system, and it was not officially used in France until after his death in 1852. Today, however, braille is used all over the world, and it has been adapted for many languages, including Japanese.
You may have seen braille in your daily life. In Japan, it can be found on train ticket machines and elevator buttons. It is even printed on the tops of beer cans, so that people do not mistake them for soft drinks.

qs.q: How many dots are used to make each letter?
qs.ex: Each letter is made of up to six dots とあります。

qs.q: What was the problem with the books at Louis's school?
o: They were heavy and slow to read.
They were written in a foreign language.
They were too expensive for students.
qs.ex: which were heavy and very slow to read とあります。

qs.q: Where did Louis get the idea for his system?
o: From a system soldiers had used at night.
qs.ex: a system of dots that soldiers had used to read messages at night とあります。

qs.q: What happened after Louis created his system?
o: It was used in France immediately.
He changed it for the Japanese language.
Many teachers did not accept it at first.
qs.ex: At first, many teachers did not accept Louis's system とあります。

qs.q: Which of the following statements is true?
o: Braille can only be used for letters.
Braille is used on elevator buttons in Japan.
Louis created his system when he was 20.
Braille is used only in France.
qs.ex: In Japan, it can be found on ... elevator buttons とあります。数字や音符にも使え、完成は15歳のときです。

parts.prompt:
以下の英文を読んで、その内容を英語で要約し、解答欄に記入しなさい。
語数の目安は25語〜35語です。
parts.body:
At many train stations in Japan, people usually stand on one side of the escalator and leave the other side open for people who want to walk. Recently, however, some stations have started asking people to stand on both sides and not to walk.
Station staff say that walking on escalators is dangerous, because people can fall or bump into others. Also, when everyone stands on both sides, more people can use the escalator at the same time, so lines become shorter.
On the other hand, people who are in a hurry feel that standing still is too slow. In addition, it is difficult to change a habit that many people have had for a long time.
rules: 解答は、英文要約の解答欄に書きなさい。なお、解答欄の外に書かれたものは採点されません。
要約の内容が英文から逸れていると判断された場合は、0点と採点されることがあります。英文をよく読んでから答えてください。
parts.model: Some stations ask people not to walk on escalators and to stand on both sides. This prevents accidents and moves more people. However, busy people find it slow, and habits are hard to change.
checks: 第1段落(エスカレーターで両側に立ち、歩かないようにたのむ駅がある)の内容が入っている
第2段落(良い点:事故を防ぐ・多くの人が使える)の内容が入っている
第3段落(悪い点:急ぐ人にはおそい・習慣を変えにくい)の内容が入っている
本文の文をそのまま写さず、自分の言葉で短くまとめている
語数が25〜35語になっている
parts.title: ライティング(英文要約)

parts.prompt:
以下のQUESTIONについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ書きなさい。

QUESTION
Do you think cities should have more bike lanes?
rules: 語数の目安は50語〜60語です。
理由は2つ書きましょう。
QUESTIONに答えていない場合や、内容がQUESTIONからずれている場合は、0点と採点されることがあります。
parts.model: I think cities should have more bike lanes. First, riding a bike on the road with cars is dangerous, so special lanes would protect cyclists and reduce accidents. Second, if cycling becomes safer, more people will choose bikes instead of cars, and this will reduce traffic and air pollution. Therefore, I agree with this idea.
checks: 最初に賛成か反対かをはっきり書いている
理由に具体的な説明がある
語数が50〜60語になっている
スペルや文法のミスがない
parts.title: ライティング(英作文)

lines: Hi, Mike. Do you want to go to the new ramen shop near the station after school?
I'd love to, but I have basketball practice until six.
Saturday is perfect. Let's meet in front of the station at noon.
items.q: Where will they meet?
items.ex: Let's meet in front of the station at noon. と言っています。

lines: Excuse me, does this bus go to the stadium?
No, you need the number 12. This is the number 21.
Oh, I see. Where can I catch the number 12?
At the bus stop across the street.
items.q: What is the man's problem?
o: He is about to take the wrong bus.
He doesn't know the name of the stadium.
items.ex: スタジアムへは12番のバスで、これは21番。乗るバスがちがいます。

lines: Dad, I want to get a part-time job at the convenience store.
What about your studies? Your exams are next month.
OK, but you should start after your exams.
items.q: What does the father say?
o: She can't get a job at all.
She should work at a different store.
She should wait until after her exams.
items.ex: you should start after your exams(試験のあとで始めなさい)と言っています。

lines: Hello, I'd like to send this package to Canada.
Would you like to send it by air or by sea?
How long does it take by sea?
About two months. By air, it takes about a week.
I'll send it by air, then. It's a birthday present.
items.q: Why does the man send the package by air?
items.ex: 誕生日プレゼントなので、早く届く航空便にしました。

lines: Have you seen my glasses? I can't find them anywhere.
Did you look in the living room?
Oh, wait. They're on your head!
items.q: Where are the woman's glasses?
items.ex: They're on your head! と言っています。

lines: Ms. White, I'm sorry, but I left my homework at home.
That's the second time this week, Ryan.
I know. I'll bring it tomorrow.
All right. But please put it in your bag the night before.
items.q: What does the teacher tell Ryan to do?
o: Put his homework in his bag the night before.
items.ex: please put it in your bag the night before と言っています。

lines: Welcome to City Bike Rental. How can I help you?
I'd like to rent a bike for the day.
That's 15 dollars. You need to bring it back by 6 p.m.
You'll have to pay an extra five dollars.
items.q: What will happen if the man returns the bike after 6 p.m.?
o: He will pay five dollars more.
He can't rent a bike again.
items.ex: You'll have to pay an extra five dollars. と言っています。

lines: Did you watch the soccer game last night?
No, I fell asleep before it started. Who won?
Japan won two to one. The last goal was in the final minute.
Wow, I wish I had seen it.
items.q: What does the woman say?
o: She wishes she had seen the game.
items.ex: I wish I had seen it.(見ればよかった)と言っています。

lines: Excuse me, I'd like to change my seat. The person in front of me is too tall, and I can't see the stage.
Let me check. There's an empty seat in the third row.
items.q: Why does the woman want to change her seat?
o: It is too close to the stage.
Her friend is sitting in the third row.
items.ex: 前の人の背が高くて舞台が見えないからです。

lines: Mom, can we get a cat?
You know your father is allergic to cats.
That's a good idea. Fish are easier to take care of, too.
items.q: Why can't they get a cat?
o: The father is allergic to cats.
items.ex: your father is allergic to cats と言っています。

lines: Hi, I'm calling about the yoga classes I saw on your website.
Yes. We have classes for beginners on Tuesdays and Fridays.
Can I try a class before I sign up?
Of course. The first class is free. How about this Friday?
items.q: What will the woman do on Friday?
items.ex: 最初のクラスは無料で、今週の金曜日に体験します。

lines: How did you like the Italian restaurant?
The pasta was delicious, but the service was slow. We waited 40 minutes for our food.
I'd go again for the food, though.
items.q: What did the woman think about the restaurant?
items.ex: the service was slow と言っています。パスタはおいしかったのです。

lines: Grandpa, can you teach me how to play chess?
Of course. Do you know how the pieces move?
Let's start with that, then. I'll get the board.
items.q: What will they do first?
items.ex: 駒の動かし方から始めようと言っています。

lines: Excuse me, I'm looking for the post office. Is it near here?
It used to be on this street, but it moved last year.
It's next to the city hall. Go straight two blocks and turn left.
items.q: Where is the post office now?
items.ex: It's next to the city hall. と言っています。前はこの通りにありました。

lines: Sorry. My alarm clock didn't ring this morning.
You should use your phone as an alarm, too.
That's a good idea. I'll set two alarms from now on.
items.q: What will Jessica do from now on?
items.ex: I'll set two alarms from now on. と言っています。

lines: Every year, Mai's school holds a recycling contest. Each class collects plastic bottles and cans for one month. This year, Mai's class collected the most, and they won a trip to an aquarium. Mai said that she now thinks more carefully about what she throws away.
items.q: What did Mai's class win?
items.ex: they won a trip to an aquarium とあります。

lines: Attention, passengers on Flight 305 to Sydney. The departure gate has been changed from Gate 12 to Gate 28. Boarding will begin at 3:15 p.m. Please go to Gate 28 now.
items.q: What has changed?
items.ex: 搭乗口が12番から28番に変わりました。

lines: Owls can turn their heads about 270 degrees. This is because they cannot move their eyes like humans can. By turning their heads, they can look around without moving their bodies, which helps them catch small animals at night.
items.q: Why do owls turn their heads so far?
items.ex: they cannot move their eyes like humans can とあります。

lines: Jake started a vegetable garden on his balcony last spring. He grew tomatoes, peppers, and herbs. At first, many of his plants died because he gave them too much water. Now he checks the soil before watering, and his tomatoes are growing well.
items.q: Why did many of Jake's plants die at first?
o: He gave them too much water.
items.ex: because he gave them too much water とあります。

lines: Welcome to Pine Hill Library. Starting next month, you can borrow up to ten books at a time, instead of five. Also, our new study room on the third floor is now open. Please reserve it at the front desk.
items.q: What will change next month?
items.ex: 来月から5冊ではなく10冊まで借りられます。自習室はすでに開いています。

lines: In the past, people in Japan used furoshiki, a large square cloth, to wrap and carry things. Today, furoshiki are becoming popular again because they can be used many times instead of plastic bags. Some stores even give a discount to customers who bring their own furoshiki.
items.q: Why are furoshiki becoming popular again?
o: They can be used many times.
They are sold only in Japan.
items.ex: they can be used many times instead of plastic bags とあります。

lines: Hannah wanted to run a full marathon. She trained for a year, running a little farther every week. During the race, she hurt her ankle, but she did not give up. She walked the last ten kilometers and finished the race in six hours.
items.q: What did Hannah do after she hurt her ankle?
items.ex: She walked the last ten kilometers and finished the race とあります。

lines: Good evening, everyone, and thank you for coming to tonight's concert. Before we begin, please turn off your phones. Taking photos and videos is not allowed. There will be a 15-minute break after the first half.
items.q: What are people asked to do?
items.ex: please turn off your phones とあります。

lines: Paul is a pilot for an airline. Before every flight, he checks the weather along the route and talks with the other pilot about the plan. He says that the most important part of his job is good communication with the crew.
items.q: What does Paul think is most important in his job?
items.ex: the most important part of his job is good communication with the crew とあります。

lines: Sea otters often hold hands while they sleep. They do this so that they do not drift away from each other in the water. Sea otters also wrap themselves in seaweed to stay in one place.
items.q: Why do sea otters hold hands while sleeping?
items.ex: so that they do not drift away from each other(はなれないように)とあります。

lines: Thank you for calling Blue Sky Travel. Our office is now closed. Our business hours are from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., Monday to Saturday. If you need to change a flight urgently, please visit our website.
items.q: What should callers do if they need to change a flight urgently?
items.ex: please visit our website とあります。

lines: Aiko is a junior high school student who loves K-pop. She wanted to understand the songs better, so she started studying Korean. She practices by watching Korean dramas with subtitles. Next year, she hopes to visit Seoul with her family.
items.q: How does Aiko practice Korean?
o: She writes letters to a friend.
She watches Korean dramas with subtitles.
items.ex: She practices by watching Korean dramas with subtitles. とあります。

lines: Some hotels in Japan offer capsule rooms. Each capsule is just big enough for one person to sleep in. They are cheaper than regular hotel rooms, so they are popular with business people who miss the last train and with travelers on a budget.
items.q: Why are capsule hotels popular with some travelers?
o: They are cheaper than regular hotels.
items.ex: They are cheaper than regular hotel rooms とあります。

lines: Attention, all shoppers. Our store will be closing in fifteen minutes. Please bring your items to the registers on the first floor. The registers on the second floor are already closed. Thank you for shopping with us.
items.q: Where should shoppers pay?
items.ex: 2階のレジはもう閉まっているので、1階のレジへ。

lines: Ben wanted to learn how to swim before his family trip to Okinawa. He took lessons at the city pool twice a week. At first, he was afraid of putting his face in the water. By the time of the trip, he could swim twenty-five meters.
items.q: How far could Ben swim by the time of the trip?
items.ex: By the time of the trip, he could swim twenty-five meters. とあります。
